This is a 40-year-old AFAB patient with a 5-month history of bladder-centered irritative symptoms: suprapubic discomfort *relieved by voiding*, urinary frequency (10–15/day), nocturia (2–3×), and dyspareunia — all in the absence of dysuria, hematuria, fever, or systemic illness. All major alternative diagnoses (UTI, structural disease, gynecologic pathology, neurologic disorder) are robustly excluded by objective data. The presence of dyspareunia further aligns with IC/BPS, as trigonal and bladder base involvement commonly refers pain to the vaginal introitus.
